A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BNEM research. Their methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V4 reports original NEM/BNEM sampling experiments on four benchmark potentials, alongside appendix ablations, estimator analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V5 retains these original experiments and adds HMC/Parallel Tempering comparisons and GPU-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The estimators, losses, networks, iterative training, and bootstrap rejection procedure are retained, including ME-NEM and TweeDEM. The Gaussian-center correction in Eq. (15) matches the estimator already specified in v4's appendix; the expanded normalization explanation does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: GMM-40, DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55, and the auxiliary ten-mode GMM variance analysis are retained. The new HMC/PT comparison uses the existing GMM-40 and DW-4 tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix M.9 and Table 12 add evaluated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Parallel Tempering baselines on GMM-40 and DW-4. Existing neural-baseline comparisons, including the appendix iEFM comparisons, are retained.

E3.justification: The new HMC/PT experiment introduces 100/1000 energy-evaluation budgets and step-size sweeps selected using E-W2. V5 also introduces fixed-batch sampling-memory measurements. Existing benchmark metrics, training settings, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M.5 adds measured GPU-memory overhead to the existing computational-cost analysis. The earlier smoothing, sample-budget, noise-schedule, outlier, and estimator bias/variance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains three-seed mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and the same convergence flags. Table 12 also averages three seeds without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure. The altered uncertainty value in Table 4 is a numerical edit, not a reporting-practice change.

E6.justification: New Tables 8 and 12 report GPU-memory measurements and HMC/PT scores; LJ-55 sampling memory is 1.30 GiB for iDEM versus 4.30 GiB for NEM/BNEM. Table 1 is unchanged. Table 4 changes iDEM-100's printed LJ-13 E-W2 uncertainty from 590,290 to 590 while retaining the mean 1190.59; the reason is not stated.

T1.justification: V5 adds O(1/K) remainders to Propositions 3.1 and 3.3 and explicitly qualifies Proposition 3.4's bootstrap formulas as approximate. Appendices C, D, E, and G revise supporting derivations, including triangle-inequality, noise-covariance, and bootstrap exponential/remainder corrections. The existing theoretical framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about energy matching, bootstrap variance reduction, empirical advantages, and robustness across four benchmark tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix M.9 adds interpretations of HMC's mode-weighting difficulties and PT's response to increased sampling budgets. Appendix B.2 expands the heuristic rationale for loss normalization and rejection. The existing differentiation-memory and spline-bias limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V5 specifies memory-profiling batch sizes of 1024, 1024, 128, and 128 and adds an anonymous implementation-reference link in Section 5. Existing architecture descriptions, training hyperparameters, hardware disclosure, GitHub link, and asset licenses are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning through discussions of adjoint/Schrödinger-bridge samplers, annealing and trust-region methods, and energy-based training regularizers. It adds multiple contemporary works and explains their relationship to possible NEM/BNEM extensions, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V5 expands selected training and proof explanations, edits the conclusion and author information, and removes the appendix contents list. The principal narrative and the organization of retained technical material remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted for TMLR, changing typography, margins, headers, author layout, and float placement. Figures 4–5 move from text-wrapped displays to a shared row, and two tables are added. Figure 5's revised caption clarifies logarithmic axes already present in v4.

improvement.justification: More explicit theoretical qualifications and corrected derivation steps improve precision. The memory measurements, conventional-sampler comparisons, and updated related work strengthen transparency and context. These gains are limited: the new HMC/PT evidence covers two retained tasks and provides only abbreviated tuning details, while the main experimental findings remain unchanged.
